description: New in TD 2025.3: Writes POP contents to Alembic .abc files. Supports multi-frame animation, built-in and custom attributes, and multiple POPs as separate Alembic objects in one file. Enables pipeline integration with Houdini, Maya, Blender, and other 3D software.

parameters.name: File Path
parameters.description: Output file path for the .abc Alembic file. Use $F for frame number substitution.

parameters.name: Record
parameters.description: When enabled, continuously writes frames to the Alembic file each cook.

parameters.name: Output Object Name
parameters.description: Name of the Alembic object created from this POP's data. Multiple POPs can use different names in one file.

parameters.name: Attributes
parameters.description: Which attribute classes to include in the export. Custom lets you specify exact attributes.

parameters.name: Custom Attributes
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of attribute names to export when Attributes is set to Custom.

parameters.name: Include Velocity
parameters.description: When enabled, exports velocity (v) attribute for motion blur compatibility in other DCCs.

parameters.name: Frame Range
parameters.description: Frame range to record when Record is disabled. Format: start-end or start-end:step.

useCases: Exporting POP simulations to Alembic for rendering in other 3D software
Caching POP animations to disk for playback without re-cooking
Pipeline integration with Houdini, Maya, and Blender via Alembic
Recording real-time POP output for post-production
Sharing POP-generated geometry across multiple applications
Archiving interactive installation states for later playback

troubleshooting.problem: Alembic file is empty or has no geometry
troubleshooting.solution: Verify the input POP chain has valid geometry with points and primitives. Check that File Path is writable and the directory exists.
Set Attributes to 'All' or 'Custom' with the specific attribute names. Some attributes may not transfer if they are the wrong class (point vs vertex vs primitive).

troubleshooting.problem: Alembic file can't be read by other software
troubleshooting.solution: Ensure the Alembic file is written with standard Ogawa format. Some older DCC versions may need the legacy HDF5 format.

troubleshooting.problem: Performance issues when recording many frames
troubleshooting.solution: Reduce the number of attributes exported (use Custom mode with only needed attributes). Consider recording at a lower frame rate and interpolating in the DCC.
